digest.component_or_area: completion-verifier agent step, pydantic-ai tool-call boundary
propositions: The primary completion-verify agent step is dispatched with no forced-landing boundary (tool_step_limit never set), allowing budget exhaustion to kill the run and emit no verdict instead of landing one on gathered evidence.

Runaway tool-call cycles (k-cycles with k≥2) go undetected because max_consecutive_repeat only counts adjacent identical calls, scoring a 4-call cycle as 1 and missing non-adjacent repetition entirely.

When the verifier exhausts its step budget mid-loop, UsageLimitExceeded→LLMRunnerError is not caught by CompletionAgentStep (only UnretryableOutputError caught), so bounded recovery is unreachable and the run terminates with no verdict and no gate_error_v1 sidecar.

A windowed distinct-ratio metric (trailing 24 tool calls, trip at ≤0.50) discriminates pathological runs (ratio 0.031–0.290 across measured loops) from healthy breadth (ratio 0.833–1.000) and is implementable without re-walking full message history.

Four real occurrences now demonstrate the loop is reproducible, scale-independent, and affects small tickets (aec1, 895c: no descendants) to large epics (e369: 59 descendants), forcing unattested force-close exits despite tickets meeting their acceptance criteria.
